newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz seen posting strong 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Allianz seen posting strong 1996 earnings.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding is poised to make good its pledge of a substantial rise in pre-tax profits in 1996, although its future earnings outlook may be more moderate, analysts said on Monday.

Allianz, which reports preliminary profit data on Wednesday, is expected to reap the benefits of favourable market conditions and modest claims although a sharp rise in tax charges will cap its earnings growth on a net basis.
Forecasts for its pre-tax profit range from 3.45 to 3.80 billion marks ($2.0-2.2 billion), representing increases of between 13 and 25 percent from the record 3.04 billion-mark level of 1995.

"The company has made very clear its claims situation has improved," said Joerg Schuster, an analyst at Independent Research in Frankfurt, whose forecasts for Allianz's 1996 performance -- with estimated EPS of 92 marks after 87.20 in 1995 -- are at the top end of the scale.

"Profits will not have risen into infinity but it does look positive," said WestLB analyst Georg Kanders, who recently raised his recommendation on Allianz to "buy" and expects the group's underwriting earnings and investment returns to improve substantially.
Allianz's net earnings, burdened by a sharp rise in taxation levels after the group used a tax break in 1995, are generally expected to increase by under 10 percent.
Estimates for after-tax profit range from 2.1 to 2.3 billion marks after 2.02 billion the previous year -- based on assumptions of a tax rate of above 40 percent compared with 34 percent in 1995.
Analysts were divided on Allianz's future prospects with some saying its share price would be pressured once German interest rates were increased from their current historic lows.
Allianz shares, which closed bourse trade Monday at 3,268 marks, have risen some 17 percent this year compared with a 12 percent advance by the blue chip DAX index.

"In the medium term Allianz is not going to be an outperformer," said BHF-Bank AG analyst Dieter Hein, who is forecasting 1996 pre-tax profit of 3.75 billion marks and net profit of 2.2 billion marks.
"The insurance sector has been seeing good rise in premiums and a strong claims environment for several years. But this time is now past," Hein said.
"We are seeing pressure on the motor side and in non-life insurance in general and the claims situation is likely to stagnate or get worse," he added.

Independent Research's Schuster noted that Allianz was still suffering from weak home business, where deregulation has led to fierce pressure on non-life insurance business, although he predicted the situation would ease in 1997.
Allianz's premium income was likely to rise only one percent at home in 1996, he said, although foreign business should improve more strongly.
However analysts were generally upbeat on the company's recent efforts to restructure its operations.

"It's good to see Allianz taking more control of its French operations and other units should provide good synergies," said Patrizia Novak of Commerzbank AG of Allianz increasing its stake to 99 percent in loss-making French unit Allianz Via. He has a "hold" recommendation on Allianz.
Allianz last year consolidated its Swiss Berner insurance unit and credit insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG and sold off its health insurance unit Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG.
Its new health unit, Vereinte, acquired last year in a complex share swap with Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, is being consolidated in the current year.
Allianz itself has said the restructuring shaved 200 million marks off its premium income in the first nine months of 1996, of a total of 56.2 billion marks.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.692 German Marks)
